title.narrative: Garantifacilitet i Palestina, SGF1 fas II Gåvodel
Swedish Guarantee Facility in Palestine, SGF1 phase II Grant part

description.narrative: Garantifacilitet i Palestina, fas två. Gåvodelen täcker både administration av garantin och tekniskt stöd till låntagare.
Guarantee Facility in Palestine, phase II. The grant part includes both the administration of the guarantee and the technical assistance to borrowers.
i) Increased access to credit for SMEs in East Jerusalem, Area C and Gaza and for SMEs run by women in the whole of Palestine ii) Improved financial literacy and transparency of Palestinian SMEs

Some highlights from the reporting period starting in January 2017 through end of May 2021. - 649 SME loans in the amount of $52,369,022 were processed by MEII staff. - 556 SME loans totaling $41,244,537 were approved. -93 SME loans totaling $11,124,485 were rejected by MEII or withdrawn by the banks. - 16 Demands for Payment totaling $230,015 were submitted and settled under SGF. - The SGF portfolio (outstanding) consisted of 311 loans in the amount of $13,091,994 of which Sida's share of risk exposure amounted to $8,909,296. - 808 SMEs registered on Tamweeli. - 116 university interns were trained by MEII, out of which 69 received post internship employment. - 797 accounting software applications were installed, and 82% of previously installed accounting software licenses were renewed by the SMEs - 2,524 jobs sustained by SGF, and 116 new jobs under TAP. - 42% of the loans it has guaranteed to date went to new borrowers (i.e. SMEs that did not have a formal bank loan). This is a significant indicator about the impact SGF is having on the marginalized areas, and a core objective of MEIIs attempts for financial inclusion.
Due to the deteriorating economic situation only 1% of loans were made without commercial risk coverage against a target of 8%. The 1% represents loans that were rejected by MEII under SGF but which the lenders decided to proceed on without SGF coverage. The low percentage indicates the strong reluctance of banks to lend in the marginalized communities. Only $5.98 million in Tamweeli loans were financed against a target of $11.35 million. The weakening economic conditions especially in 2020 following the COVID19 pandemic but also prior to the pandemic, and mainly in Gaza where banks more or less stopped lending, had an impact on Tamweeli funding requests.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
